title: Lab 1: A 4-bit shift register on the FPGA
summary: Describe a 4-bit **serial-in, parallel-out** shift register in SystemVerilog, simulate it, and run it on the board: a push button is the clock, a switch the serial input, four LEDs show the register.
objectives: Verify a design with a self-checking testbench
Map ports to pins and program the board

steps.title: Create the Vivado project
steps.md: Create an **RTL project** for your board. Download the lab files (**Files** tab → *Download all*) and add `src/rtl/*.sv` as design sources and `src/sim/tb_shift4.sv` as a simulation source.

steps.title: Write the shift register
steps.md: Describe the register with one `always_ff` block. On reset all bits are 0; otherwise the bits move one place and `d_in` enters at bit 0.
steps.hint: The concatenation `{q[2:0], d_in}` builds the new 4-bit value.

steps.title: Simulate with a testbench
steps.md: Write `tb_shift4.sv`: 10 ns clock, reset for two cycles, shift in **1, 0, 1, 1** and check `q == 4'b1011` with an assertion.

steps.title: Debounce the button
steps.md: Add `debounce.sv`: accept a new button level only after it was stable for **10 ms**. Drive the shift-register clock from its output.

steps.title: Constraints, implementation and timing
steps.md: Map `BTN0 → btn`, `SW0 → d_in`, `LED0..3 → q[0..3]`. Run implementation and check that the timing summary has **no failing paths**.

steps.title: Run it on the board
steps.md: Program the device. Set SW0, press the button, and watch the bit move along the LEDs. After 1, 0, 1, 1 the LEDs show `1011`.

questions.text: What does `q <= {q[2:0], d_in};` do on a clock edge?
options: Shifts the bits one place and puts `d_in` into bit 0

questions.text: Why must the push button be debounced before it is used as a clock?
options: A bouncing button produces several edges per press
Without debouncing the register may shift more than once per press
Debouncing is needed only in simulation

questions.text: Put the design steps in order.
After shifting in 1, 0, 1, 1, what do the LEDs `q[3:0]` show?
